questions.q_en: Find the angle between the hands of the clock when the time is 09:36.
questions.solution_en:
The angle between the hour hand and minute hand can be calculated using the formula -

Angle = |(60H - 11M)/2|

Where, H = Hour and M = Minutes

Here H = 9 and M = 36

Angle = |(60 X 9 - 11 X 36)/2|

= |(540 - 396)/2|

= |(144)/2|

= |72|

Angle = 72°

Find the sum of the shortest distance between D and J and the shortest distance between P and Z in the given expression P(10+10)D(4-1)W(4=4)Z(10@3)J^W^D?
questions.solution_en:
It is given that,

'A(1+1)B' means 'A stands 2m to the north of B'

'A(2@2)B' means 'A stands 4m to the west of B'

'A(7=1)B' means 'A stands 8m to the east of B'

'A(5-5)B' means 'A stands 10m to the south of B'

'A^B^C' means 'Persons A, B and C form an equilateral triangle'

The given expression is: P(10+10)D(4-1)W(4=4)Z(10@3)J^W^D

Thus, we have:

P is 20m to the north of D.

D is 5m to the south of W.

W is 8m to the east of Z.

Z is 13m to the west of J.

J, W and D form an isosceles right angled triangle.

The distance between D and J is 5√2m.

The distance between Z and P = 82+152 = 289 = 17m.

So, the total distance = 17+5√2 = (17+5√2)m

In a row, Gopal is standing 16th from the right end and Usha is standing at the right end of a row.

Gopal (16th from right end) - 14 persons - Usha.

15 persons are standing between Gopal and Mohan.

Mohan - 15 persons - Gopal (16th from right end) - 14 persons - Usha.

Persons standing between Mohan and Usha = 15+Gopal+14 = 30 persons
